history.period: 14th century CE (built 1338 CE per most sources; one source says 1342 CE — CONFLICT (verify))
history.summary: Stone temple built in 1338 CE (popularly dated) at Sringeri in the Sringeri Sharada Peetham complex, dedicated to Vidyashankara (Vidyatirtha), the 10th Jagadguru of the peetham. Tradition holds that Vidyaranya influenced Harihara and Bukka, founders of the Vijayanagara Empire, to build it over his guru's samadhi. Built entirely of stone in a fusion of Hoysala/Chalukya and Dravidian styles on a star-shaped plinth, with a famous 12-pillared mandapa whose pillars align with the zodiac (sunlight falls on the month's pillar), and basement friezes depicting Puranic stories and the Dashavatara. George Michell notes 16th-century additions. It is a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Vidyashankara Temple
town_description: Sringeri is a temple town on the banks of the Tunga river in the Malnad region at the foothills of the Western Ghats. It is the site of the first and southernmost of the four cardinal peethams established by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century, and the headquarters of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham. The town lies about 90 km west of Chikkamagaluru and 336 km from Bengaluru.

travel.road: Well connected by road; Sringeri is ~90 km west of Chikkamagaluru on the Malnad route, ~336 km from Bengaluru. Temple is within the Sringeri Sharada Peetham complex.
